# I Know What I Saw

It was tall, it was in a hurry, and it was gone before I found my camera. I'm writing it down
anyway. This is the first entry in my field notes.

It's also your first post. Every Markdown file in `src/posts/` is a post: `posts.json` gives
them all the layout and the `posts` tag, so they show up on the home page, newest first.

Edit this file while `ssqch serve` is running, and the page reloads by itself.

---
url: https://example.com/posts/raiders-of-the-lost-path/
---

# Raiders of the Lost Path

A ranger came by with an old map of these notes. It pointed to a heading called "The tracks".
I had renamed it "Where they lead" the week before. The ranger was not pleased, and neither
was the build.

## What the build said

The link checker (`linksPlugin()` in `ssqch.config.js`) follows every link inside the site
after a production build. A link to a page that isn't there, or to a heading that isn't on it,
fails the build and says where:

```text
error: after_build hook failed: the trail goes cold on 1 broken link:
  /posts/i-know-what-i-saw/ -> /posts/the-stump-has-moved/#the-tracks (no id "the-tracks" on that page)
```

## The correction

A heading's id comes from its text, so renaming a heading moves its address. Point the link at
the new one, `#where-they-lead`, or keep the old heading. In `ssqch serve` it's a warning, so
you can keep writing while you look for it.

This link works, for comparison: [back to what the build said](#what-the-build-said).

---
url: https://example.com/posts/the-cache-of-the-wild/
---

# The Cache of the Wild

The raccoon keeps a dated copy of the trail conditions. He checks the ranger station once a
day, and the rest of the time he reads you his copy. When the station doesn't answer, he reads
you his copy anyway and mentions how old it is.

A data file that asks a server for something can do the same. Save this as
`src/_data/conditions.js`, and every page has `conditions`:

```js
export default async function () {
  // Asked once a day; until then, the saved copy in .cache/ssqch/fetch/.
  const response = await fetch("https://api.example.com/trails/cedar", { cache: "1d" });
  return response.json();
}
```

- While `ssqch serve` rebuilds on every save, the server is asked once a day, not once a save.
- When the server is down and there's a copy, the build uses it and says how old it is.
- `ssqch build --offline` uses only the saved copies, whatever their age, so a build on a plane
  never touches the network.

The raccoon has never been on a plane. He has opinions about the Old Growth trail.

# The Stump Has Moved

I went back a third time. The stump is gone. There are tracks.

More as it develops. To start an entry of your own:

```sh
ssqch new posts --title "My second sighting"
```

It copies `src/_blueprints/posts.md` and fills in the title and today's date. Add
`draft: true` to a post's front matter to keep it out of production builds until you're sure
of what you saw.

---
url: https://example.com/posts/upon-further-review-a-stump/
---

# Upon Further Review, a Stump

I went back in daylight. It was a stump. A tall one, to be fair to me.

The `description` in this post's front matter is the page's meta description; posts without
one get the site's, from `src/_data/site.json`.

I didn't take a picture, since it was a stump. When you have one worth showing, save it as
`src/img/stump.jpg` and write `![The stump](/img/stump.jpg)`. The build turns it into a
`<picture>` in three sizes, so it stays sharp on any screen. Whether it was sharp to begin
with is between you and your camera.

A raccoon who keeps everything told me the trick for deploying: keep `dist/img/` and
`.cache/` between builds, and the build never encodes the same picture twice. Raccoon's cache.
Raccoon did not see anything tall.
